name: Environment-Illumination
description: Too much or too little light that was a negative influence on vision.

name: Environment-Weather / wind / turbulence
description: Assessment of the weather - consider condensation, fog, frost, hail, ice, mist rain, sleet, snow, excessive wind/ gusts.

name: Environment-Temperature / humidity
description: Extreme of heat, cold, and humidity that may have a negative influence on human or equipment performance.

name: Environment-Contaminants
description: Consider if any contaminants were present, e.g. carbon dioxide, carbon monoxide, chemicals, dust, foreign objects, debris, mists, smog, smoke, toxic materials, or vapours

name: Environment-Noise
description: Was there excessive noise? Did it interfere with communication?

name: Environment-Vibration
description: Assessment of vibration in the area.

name: Environment-Acceleration / deceleration
description: Consider acceleration experienced by personnel/equipment

name: Environment-Radiation
description: Radiant energy emitted in waves or particles that may have negative influence on human or equipment performance. This includes assessment of any potential radiation sources e.g. ionizing, laser, non-ionizing, radio waves, sunlight, ultraviolet, or X radiation.

name: Environment-Work surface/space
description: Conditions of the work surfaces on which personnel and equipment operate that may have a negative influence on performance. This includes holes, inclines, rocky, rough, rutted, slippery, steep or uneven wave action

name: Environment-Electricity
description: Assessment of any potential electrical energy sources that may have played a role in the incident.

name: Environment-Air pressure
description: Assessment of any sudden or gradual changes in air pressure that may have had a negative influence on human or equipment performance.

name: Environment-Wildlife
description: The actions or presence of animals that injure personnel, cause personnel to make errors,  damage equipment, or cause equipment to malfunction

name: Equipment-Design
description: The design of the equipment should be adequate to meet the requirements and operational conditions under which they were being used.

name: Equipment-Construction
description: The equipment should be constructed to specifications within the design standard.

name: Equipment-Testing
description: The equipment should be tested to ensure that it meets the design standard and construction specifications.

name: Equipment-Inspection
description:
There should be an inspection procedure for monitoring the status of the equipment on:
Initial Delivery
Periodically through out its life at critical times before, during and after operation

name: Equipment-Maintenance
description: The equipment should be maintained to the manufacturer's specifications to maintained the original design performance safety and reliability standards.

name: Equipment-Modification / Management of Change
description:
Equipment modification should be carried out under a "management of change" process to ensure performance, safety and reliability are not adversely affected.
Modifications should also account for changes to:
- maintenance procedures,
- inspection procedures,
- ergonomics,
- man-machine interface.

name: Procedures-Utilization
description: Documented procedures should be used for conducting the operation in a correct, safe and efficient manner.

name: Procedures-Content
description:
The documented procedures should be adequate for the scope of the work to be conducted. The procedure should:
- cover all tasks
- be tactically correct correct
- contain emergency provisions
- contain work-around provisons
- cover exemptions where the entire procedure does not apply.

name: Procedures-Criteria
description: The procedures should contain the necessary information in a user friendly language. The format should successfully link people and equipment to provide a risk minimised or risk eliminated operation.

name: Procedures-Validated
description: The procedures should be reviewed, checked and tested by qualified people to ensure that the personnel that use the procedure can carry out the operation correctly, safely, efficiently, and with minimal environmental impact.

name: Organisation-Organisational Culture
description:
The organisation should have a systematic approach to safety. There should be evidence of management leadership and commitment to setting high standards of HSEC, quality and productivity performance.
Measurable factors include:
- organisational structure,
- people management,
- provision and quality of tools and equipment,
- commercial and operational perssures,
- planning, 
- maintenance of facilities and equipment,
- communication.

name: Organisation-Training programme
description: The organisation should have a structured training programme for the provison and consolidation of technical skills, safety awareness and safety knowledge. The effectiveness of training should be measurable.

name: Organisation-Visible support
description: The organisation should demonstrate support for the work site operational staff including provision of adequate manning levels, suitable equipment and material and adequate facilities and services.

name: Organisation-Operational feedback processes
description: The organisation should have a formal and effective operational feedback system for monitoring and improvement.
